editorial:
You are dropped into a lonely moon base where Sam Bell counts down his last three weeks before heading home. With only his computer helper GERTY for company, the quiet routine feels eerie and tense. When an accident happens, things get strange fast, and you start questioning what is real. The movie moves slowly but keeps you hooked with mystery, emotion, and a strong sense of isolation.

Sam Rockwell carries almost every scene, and his performance makes you care about Sam's fear, anger, and hope. The moon setting looks real and lonely, and the simple effects work well. The pacing is slow and thoughtful, so if you want nonstop action, this may not be for you. But if you enjoy smart sci-fi with heart, it is a great pick. Watch it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: You learn Sam is not one person but a series of clones, and the company has been replacing him to keep the base running. The Sam you follow discovers another clone and fights to survive. In the end, he escapes in a pod while the other clone stays behind, and a message reaches Earth, exposing the truth to the world.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves smart, character-driven science fiction.
